title: How Many People Share Your Name?
sourceNote: Original text and visual labels transcribed from two teacher-provided classroom images. No publication date, article URL or publication credit is shown in the images.

image1.title: How Many People Share Your Name?
image1.intro: Have you ever met someone with the same name as you? Maybe even the same first AND last name? You’re not alone. Around the world, millions of people share names! Let’s dive in!
image1.heading: Do People Really Share the Same Name?
prose: Yes, and it happens a lot!
There are over 150 million Muhammads, more than 30 million Johns, and millions of girls named Maria around the world. In China alone, over 100 million people share the last name Wang!
With only so many names to go around and 8 billion people on Earth, chances are high that someone else out there has your exact name...or even thousands of them do.

researchers.heading: Researchers say:
bullets: - If your name is very common, like “John Smith,” you might share it with thousands of people (real data says over 40,000 John Smiths in the U.S. alone!).
- If your name is less common, you might share it with none or just a few.

bullets: - Over 85% of people share one of the top 100 surnames
- Only a few thousand common first names are in regular use

sentenceUnits: Have you ever met someone with the same name as you?
Maybe even the same first AND last name?
You’re not alone.
Around the world, millions of people share names!
Let’s dive in!
Yes, and it happens a lot!
There are over 150 million Muhammads, more than 30 million Johns, and millions of girls named Maria around the world.
In China alone, over 100 million people share the last name Wang!
With only so many names to go around and 8 billion people on Earth, chances are high that someone else out there has your exact name...or even thousands of them do.
Let’s take two real U.S. name lists:
Top 100 first names (like Emma, Liam, Olivia, Noah...)
Top 100 surnames (like Smith, Johnson, Brown, Garcia...)
That gives us 100 × 100 = 10,000 common full-name combinations.
But the U.S. has 330 million people, so: 330,000,000 ÷ 10,000 = 33,000 people per common name combo (on average!)
If your name is very common, like “John Smith,” you might share it with thousands of people (real data says over 40,000 John Smiths in the U.S. alone!).
If your name is less common, you might share it with none or just a few.
Things are very different here!
China has 1.4 billion people
Over 85% of people share one of the top 100 surnames
Only a few thousand common first names are in regular use
Let’s try the math:
100 common surnames × 3,000 common first names = 300,000 full-name combos. Now divide China’s population by that:
And that’s just an average.
Some names, like Wang Wei, are shared by hundreds of thousands of people!
